description.value: A case-control study comparing resting-state functional connectivity in asymptomatic MAPT mutation carriers and subjects with bvFTD with matched control groups.

spans.text: To determine whether functional connectivity is altered in subjects with mutations in the microtubule associated protein tau (MAPT) gene who were asymptomatic but were destined to develop dementia, and to compare these findings to those in subjects with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD).

description.value: Case-control study with asymptomatic MAPT subjects and matched MAPT controls, plus subjects with bvFTD and matched bvFTD controls.

model_settings.value: Two-sample two-sided t tests comparing asymptomatic MAPT subjects with MAPT controls and subjects with bvFTD with bvFTD controls; age and gender included as covariates; voxelwise results corrected at cluster level using FWE p < 0.05.

spans.text: Two-sample 2-sided t tests were performed to compare voxelwise connectivity between 1) asymptomatic MAPT subjects and MAPT controls, 2) subjects with bvFTD and bvFTD controls, and 3) asymptomatic MAPT subjects and subjects with bvFTD. These analyses were performed for both the DMN and salience networks. In order to assess only in-phase connections the group comparisons were masked by the out-of-phase connectivity map identified in a one-sample t test of the matched control group. Results were assessed at p < 0.05 corrected for multiple comparisons using FWE at the cluster level, and age and gender were included in the models as covariates.
